findings.title: Removing a client throws when V1 and V2 admin permissions are both enabled
findings.description: The listener is gated on the V1 flag (line 77), but `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is on (lines 66-71). With both flags on, a `ClientRemovedEvent` reaches `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled()`, which throws (`ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195`). `DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory.publish` calls listeners synchronously (lines 86-90), and `JpaRealmProvider` publishes the event during removal (line 1006), so client deletion fails. Before this diff the base `ClientPermissions.setPermissionsEnabled(false)` ran and succeeded. In V2-only mode the gate skips the call, which is why the new `testManageAllClients` passes. Fix: implement V2 cleanup, or have the listener skip V2 explicitly.

findings.title: Inter-client token exchange under V2 now throws instead of denying
findings.description: `canExchangeTo(client, to, token)` now throws. Its caller, `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToClient` (line 276), is reached from `V1TokenExchangeProvider` (line 154). That provider is enabled by `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` (`V1TokenExchangeProviderFactory.java:60`), and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` has no authz dependency (`Profile.java:76`), so V2 without V1 reaches this code. Before the diff, V2 used the base class, whose `canExchangeTo` returned false when no exchange policy existed, so the caller returned a clean 403. Now it returns a 500. Fix: return false, or evaluate V2 policies.

findings.title: `getClientsWithPermission` returns the type name "Clients" and never returns per-client grants
findings.description: The method calls `findByType(server, "Clients", …)`, which matches only resources whose `type` column is "Clients". Per-client resources are created without a type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104` → `JPAResourceStore.create`, lines 62-76), so they never match. Only the all-clients resource matches, so the method returns the string `"Clients"` as if it were a client id when an all-clients grant exists, and it omits every per-client grant. The base class avoids this by calling `resource.setType("Client")` (`ClientPermissions.java:131-132`). The consumer, `AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230`, calls `realm.getClientById("Clients")`, which returns null and throws an NPE. That path runs only when the V1 flag is also on (line 217). Fix: set the type on per-client resources in `getOrCreateResource`, or select by owner and map names to ids.

findings.title: Realms created before this change lack the `Clients` resource type and new scopes, and the per-client check dereferences null
findings.description: `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226-228`). It runs only when the realm attribute flips to true (`JpaClientProviderFactory.java:66-77`), and no migration calls it. Existing realms therefore never get the "Clients" resource or the CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE scopes. `getResourceTypeResource` then returns null (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:116-134`), and `findByResource(server, null)` dereferences `resource.getId()` (`JPAPolicyStore.java:215`). An admin who holds neither VIEW_CLIENTS nor MANAGE_CLIENTS and calls `canView(client)` reaches `canManage(client)` and gets a 500. Fix: null-check the fallback resource, and add an upgrade step that creates the missing type and scopes.

findings.title: The Javadoc says all-clients grants are additive, but per-client grants override them
findings.description: The Javadoc for `canManage(ClientModel)` says the V2 check is also true for an all-clients permission. The same claim appears on `canConfigure`, `canView`, and the `canMap*` methods. The implementation uses the all-clients resource only when no per-client resource exists (`ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-222`). The engine agrees: a per-client resource has no type, so `DefaultPolicyEvaluator` (lines 70-81) adds only that resource's own policies. As a result, one per-client grant on client X hides the all-clients grant on X for every other admin. The users path behaves the same way by design (`UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewUserPermissionDenyByDefault`), so the behavior may be intended. The Javadoc should say so, or the behavior should change.

findings.title: Client removal does not clean up V2 per-client grants
findings.description: V2 per-client resources are named with the client UUID (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104`), and nothing deletes them or their policies when the client is removed. In V2-only mode the listener is now gated off. Under V1+V2 it crashes (first finding). In both cases, stale resources and policies that point at deleted clients remain. Once the `getClientsWithPermission` fix lands, those stale ids would also reach the null dereference in `AvailableRoleMappingResource`.

findings.title: Display name for client permission resources is always null
findings.description: `getResourceName` has a branch only for USERS. For CLIENTS it returns `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is never set on per-client resources. `PolicyResourceService.java:218` therefore sends a null name to the admin console. Add a CLIENTS branch that returns the client's clientId, the same way the user branch returns the username.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports in `ClientPermissionsV2`
findings.description: `getEvaluationContext` is never called. It is the only user of `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, and `EvaluationContext`. The `logger` field (line 51) is unused, and so are the `Scope` import (line 27) and the static `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` import (line 46). Remove them, or wire up `getEvaluationContext` if it was meant for the token-exchange path.

findings.title: Tests miss the paths where the regressions are
findings.description: No test runs with both flags on, so nothing exercises client removal under V1+V2. Nothing exercises inter-client token exchange with V2 enabled, `getClientsWithPermission`, client display names, or a realm created before this change. The new tests do cover manage, configure, view, and map-roles for V2 clients, which is useful, but none of them reach the throwing stubs.

findings.title: Duplicated permission-evaluation loop
findings.description: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission` each repeat the same loop over `Permission.getScopes()`, and the base class already has `hasPermission(Resource, String)`. The three variants differ only in how they find the resource. A single helper that takes a `Resource` would cover all of them.

findings.title: Javadoc on `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns true"
findings.description: Both methods are `void` and throw `ForbiddenException`, but the Javadoc says "Returns {@code true}". Reword it to "Throws ForbiddenException if … returns false", matching the other `require*` docs.

findings.title: Unused test helper `createClientPolicy`
findings.description: Nothing under `tests/` calls `createClientPolicy`. Remove it, or add a test that uses it.

findings.title: Mixed JUnit 4 and 5 assertions and minor test style drift
findings.description: `PermissionClientTest` imports JUnit 4's `org.junit.Assert.fail` and also uses JUnit 5's `Assertions`. Use JUnit 5 throughout. `AbstractPermissionTest` mixes static helpers (`createAllPermission`, `createUserPolicy`) with instance overloads (`createPermission(client, …)`). `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` has many `createUserPolicy(realm, client,"…"` calls with no space after the comma, and it builds a `UserConfigBuilder` only to read an id. `AdminPermissionsSchema.java:53` has trailing whitespace.

findings.title: Inherited `require*` methods dispatch to the V2 overrides
findings.description: `requireManage()` in the base class calls `canManage()`, and `requireView(client)` calls `canView(client)`. Because `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides those methods, the inherited `require*` methods enforce the V2 rules without any duplication.
